title: HTTPS profile approval, revocation and `ward check`
description: Spec §9.1-9.2. Manifest is a request, not authority: developer approves an immutable normalized snapshot bound to project/root; any change to destination, method, auth, body or output policy, or unknown fields, invalidates it. `ward check` is local readiness only.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T13: changed URL, method, auth alias, body/output policy, binding, or unknown profile fields cannot reuse an approval
`ward check <profile> --json` reports missing binding/value/approval without any network I/O or value disclosure

plan: 1. Branch feat/WCLI-9-profile-approval off origin/dev; claim the task; record the design-settlement reading (bearer only in the first flow, non-bearer deferred) and file the deferred extension as WCLI-33.

2. Domain: a normalized approved-profile snapshot type with a discriminated auth union whose only implemented arm is bearer; normalization from the project manifest's profiles; unknown fields and unsupported auth types rejected rather than ignored.

3. Application: an approval port (developer gate, three-valued approved/declined/unavailable like the existing RegistrationApprover, never treating unavailable as consent) and a vault-backed snapshot store bound to the project and root.

4. Invalidation: at approval and at check, a declared profile must match the approved snapshot exactly on adapter, method, URL, auth scheme and alias, non-secret headers, body policy, output policy and binding; any change or unknown field refuses reuse (T13).

5. CLI: ward profile list/approve/revoke and ward check [profile] --json, local readiness only, no network I/O, no value or length or fingerprint disclosure; revocation invalidates future admissions only.
6. Tests: T13-class invalidation matrix over every snapshot field, ward check readiness and non-disclosure, unsupported-auth rejection, layer check, the full bun run check.
7. Independent review per spec 15 (opum-workflow reviewer), fix and re-verify findings, then deliver.

8. PR into dev carrying the closing evidence (PR number and CI run id, never a merge SHA), gate on every required context on the exact head SHA, squash merge, delete the local branch, and promote dev to main with git push origin origin/dev:main (main is one tracker-only commit behind and rides this promotion).
implementationNotes:
DESIGN-SETTLEMENT CHECK, RUN BEFORE STARTING (2026-09-29, at opum-agent's kickoff 03:40Z). The check was outstanding, not passed: WCLI-27's renewal note records that its session read ADR 0003 and spec 9.1-9.4 and stopped there.

QUESTION PUT: are the non-bearer auth schemes (custom API-key header, HTTP Basic) in WCLI-9 or deferred?

SOURCES READ FIRST-PARTY: WARD_MVP_AGENT_SPEC.md sections 5, 8, 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 14 and 15, and docs/adr/0003-profile-approval-authority.md read through lore. No tracker record and no doc decides the question; the spec is the only source.

READING: DEFERRED, and the spec settles it. Three clauses carry the reading. (1) 9.2 "Support Bearer authentication first", with 9.1's proposed manifest syntax declaring "auth": {"type": "bearer"}, makes bearer the first scheme and the only one the first flow names. (2) "Add a custom API-key header and HTTP Basic only if they pass the same safety tests" is conditional, and the condition is undischarged: the same safety tests are themselves being built here (T13-class approval binding, T14-class credential non-disclosure), so neither scheme can pass tests that do not exist yet. (3) "these are bounded extensions, not reasons to delay the first valid consumption flow" subordinates them to the flow, and spec 15's "Prove non-disclosure before widening the command surface" says the same. An extension is an addition to something that exists first, so it is not part of the thing it extends.

CONSEQUENCE: WCLI-9 and WCLI-10 deliver the first valid consumption flow with bearer as the only implemented scheme. The approved-snapshot schema models auth as a discriminated union so the extension is bounded, an addition rather than a migration, and an unsupported or unknown auth type is rejected at approval time under 9.2's unknown-field and no-runtime-override rules. The deferred work is filed as WCLI-33, depending on WCLI-10, with the "must pass the same safety tests" condition carried in its acceptance criteria.

ATTRIBUTION: the reading is this session's, made an execution choice by opum-agent's kickoff message conditional on the spec settling the question. It is recorded here rather than in an ADR because it decides a task boundary and not a system contract; opum-agent can correct it cheaply if it disagrees, and only WCLI-9's bearer path is built on it.
